name: zero dimensions preserve shape of nested-list storage
rectangular column stacking preserves input order
test:
import numpy as np
result = to_ndarray([np.array([1, 2]), np.array([3, 4]), np.array([5, 6])])
assert result.shape == (2, 3)
assert np.array_equal(result, [[1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6]])

name: single column retains two dimensional shape and decimal values
test:
import numpy as np
result = to_ndarray([np.array([1.25, -2.5, 0.0])])
assert result.shape == (3, 1)
assert np.array_equal(result[:, 0], [1.25, -2.5, 0.0])

name: non divisible one dimensional chunking keeps remainder
input: five elements with chunk size two
test:
import numpy as np
chunks = from_ndarray(np.arange(5), 2)
assert [part.tolist() for part in chunks] == [[0, 1], [2, 3], [4]]

name: divisible multidimensional chunking keeps whole rows
input: six by two array with chunk size three
test:
import numpy as np
source = np.arange(12).reshape(6, 2)
chunks = from_ndarray(source, 3)
assert [part.shape for part in chunks] == [(3, 2), (3, 2)]
assert np.array_equal(np.concatenate(chunks, axis=0), source)

name: large chunk and empty first axis
input: chunk larger than input, then empty array
test:
import numpy as np
assert [part.tolist() for part in from_ndarray(np.array([8, 9]), 5)] == [[8, 9]]
assert from_ndarray(np.empty((0, 2)), 3) == []
